proposals.label: Binding ban on lethal autonomous weapons
proposals.definition: Concern over weapons with increasing autonomy and calls for a legally binding instrument with prohibitions and restrictions ensuring meaningful human control over the use of force.
proposals.inclusion: Passages on killer robots, lethal autonomous weapons systems, machines deciding who lives and dies, or calls for binding rules/bans on them.
proposals.exclusion: General human control of AI outside weapons contexts (use AI_HUMAN_CONTROL_OVERSIGHT).
proposals.boundary_cases: Rhetorical questions like whether a human or a machine pulls the trigger count here when tied to weapons.

examples.quote: calling for a legally binding instrument with clear prohibitions and restrictions on autonomous weapons
stepping back from creating killing machines — lethal autonomous weapons systems — where an algorithm decides in a split second who lives and who dies
One of the most urgent threats today is the loss of human control over weapons.
Who decides whether a human being or a machine pulls the trigger?

proposals.label: Technology must remain under human control
proposals.definition: General principle that technology and algorithms must remain under human control and responsibility, beyond specific weapons rules.
proposals.inclusion: Passages asserting that algorithms must not decide alone and humans must own responsibility for technology.
proposals.exclusion: Weapons-specific human control claims (use AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS).
proposals.boundary_cases: A closing statement mixing weapons and general technology control can take both codes.

examples.quote: Technology must remain under human control. Responsibility must always be owned by us, by humans.

proposals.label: Human-centric approach and red lines
proposals.definition: New technologies including AI must respect human rights, with a human-centric approach online and offline and ethical red lines.
proposals.inclusion: Passages stating human rights apply to new technologies or calling for a human-centric approach to AI.
proposals.exclusion: Weapons-specific bans (use AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS).
proposals.boundary_cases: Red-line language introducing an autonomous weapons ban takes both codes.

examples.quote: New technologies are not a new frontier where human rights do not exist.
We have to make sure that our human-centric approach applies online and offline.

proposals.label: Technologies racing ahead, leaving many behind
proposals.definition: Concern that fast-moving technologies such as AI leave many countries or people behind.
proposals.inclusion: Passages saying AI and emerging technologies are racing ahead and leaving many behind.
proposals.exclusion: Passages focused only on rights or weapons.
proposals.boundary_cases: Brief phrasing about being left behind still counts if AI is named.

examples.quote: New and emerging technologies like artificial intelligence and quantum computing are racing ahead, leaving many of us behind.

proposals.label: Human control and safety amid racing
proposals.definition: Concern that AI governance is not keeping pace with capabilities, that humans must remain in control, and that a race for dominance could push safety aside; includes severe risks like novel pathogens and bioweapons.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on loss of human control, safety being sidelined by competitive races, governance lagging capability, or catastrophic misuse such as bioweapons.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude military-use norms (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS) and deepfake/disinformation harms (AI_DISINFORMATION).
proposals.boundary_cases: Citing warnings from the UN scientific panel about governance lag fits here and in AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: Human beings must remain in control of technology, not become a subject to it.
Nor we can allow an unchecked race for technological dominance to determine the future of AI with the pressure to move first, pushing safety, oversight, and responsibility aside.
from novel pathogens to bioweapons

proposals.label: Global rules of the road for AI
proposals.definition: Efforts to define international norms and standards for AI, including GA resolutions, and the view that governance lags development.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages on developing global AI rules, norms and standards or noting governance failing to keep pace.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude purely national measures.
proposals.boundary_cases: Mention of GA resolutions on AI also fits AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: with a view to starting to develop global rules of the road
Our ability to govern this technology is not keeping pace with its development.

proposals.label: Responsible military use of AI declaration
proposals.definition: AI's effect on warfare and political declarations on responsible military use of AI and autonomy.
proposals.inclusion: Include references to AI changing war or to military AI norms and declarations.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude bioweapon misuse, which is coded AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL.
proposals.boundary_cases: A generic 'life, work and war' phrase counts only alongside military-specific content.

examples.quote: the Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomy

proposals.label: Deepfakes and disinformation risks
proposals.definition: AI risks in the information space such as deepfakes and disinformation.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages naming deepfakes or disinformation as AI risks.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude disinformation not linked to AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: Lists mixing deepfakes with other risks count here as well.

examples.quote: But AI also brings profound risks, from deep fakes to disinformation

proposals.label: Enormous benefits versus immense harm
proposals.definition: AI framed as capable of great benefit and great harm.
proposals.inclusion: Include explicit benefit-harm pairings.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude one-sided statements.
proposals.boundary_cases: Conditional framing ('without safeguards, it can cause harm') counts.

examples.quote: AI can bring enormous benefits to humanity, but without effective safeguards, it can also cause immense harm.

proposals.label: Safety requirements for most capable models
proposals.definition: Proposals for common safety requirements for frontier AI models, including pre-release testing and reporting of serious safety failures, and capacity to assess capable systems.
proposals.inclusion: Passages calling for testing, safety standards or incident reporting for the most capable AI models.
proposals.exclusion: Weaponization of AI (use AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS).
proposals.boundary_cases: Common standards proposed via the UN take this and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: Germany calls on UN member states to work towards common safety requirements for the most capable AI models
Providers should be required to test these models before release and report serious safety failures.

proposals.label: Inclusive common rules and accountability
proposals.definition: Calls for a shared framework, common standards, oversight and accountability for AI with participation of all regions, moving beyond voluntary commitments.
proposals.inclusion: Passages on who sets AI rules, accountability, participation of all regions, oversight and common rules.
proposals.exclusion: Model-level safety testing detail (use AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL).
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements that addressing AI is a test for the UN also take AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: We need to ensure that technological progress is guided by a framework that we all have a say in shaping.
we need to ensure accountability, in particular when global peace and security are potentially affected

proposals.label: Compute access and avoiding dependencies
proposals.definition: Access to compute, data, expertise and infrastructure determines who innovates versus who accepts others' rules; cooperation should build capabilities, not dependencies.
proposals.inclusion: Passages on unequal access to AI inputs creating dependency or rule-taking.
proposals.exclusion: General digital divide statements without dependency framing (use AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE).
proposals.boundary_cases: Concern that AI cements world division if few benefit may take AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE as well.

examples.quote: Cooperation must therefore create capabilities, not new dependencies.

proposals.label: AI cementing global division
proposals.definition: AI could cement world divisions if only a few benefit, algorithms are partial, or access is limited to rich countries.
proposals.inclusion: Passages warning that AI benefits or access are limited to rich countries or few actors.
proposals.exclusion: Capacity-building programmes (use AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING).
proposals.boundary_cases: Mentions of biased algorithms in this context may also take AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.

examples.quote: it can cement the division of the world if only a few benefit from it

proposals.label: Rules on generative AI as weapon
proposals.definition: Calls for common rules on the possible use of generative AI as a weapon.
proposals.inclusion: Passages on weaponization of AI and rules against it.
proposals.exclusion: Frontier safety testing (use AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL).
proposals.boundary_cases: Accountability where global peace and security is affected may also count if weapons are implied.

examples.quote: We should also talk about common rules for the possible use of generative artificial intelligence as a weapon.

proposals.label: AI as test for UN renewal
proposals.definition: Addressing AI together is framed as a test for building a UN for today's world; institutions must catch up with AI; Global Digital Compact engagement.
proposals.inclusion: Passages linking AI governance to UN renewal or UN processes like the Global Digital Compact.
proposals.exclusion: Governance calls not tied to the UN.
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements that institutions must catch up with AI count when the UN context is explicit.

examples.quote: How we address AI together is one of the clearest tests whether we have the strength and the will to build a United Nations for today's world.
AI is not waiting for our institutions to catch up. Our institutions have to catch up with AI.

proposals.label: National AI strategy and partnership membership
proposals.definition: Speaker cites national AI achievements such as adopting an AI development strategy, joining the Global Partnership on AI, or AI becoming a national priority topic.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages reporting national AI strategies, memberships or the rising importance of AI domestically.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages where AI is only a list item of skills without national policy content.
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements that AI is 'becoming an important topic' domestically with youth investment may also be coded AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION.

examples.quote: joined the Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence and adopted a development strategy in that area back in 2019
digitalization and artificial intelligence are becoming important topics in Serbia, not just in the most developed countries of the world

proposals.label: AI listed among national youth talents
proposals.definition: AI appears in a long list of fields in which the country's young people excel, without further discussion.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages where AI is one item in a list of technologies, skills or sectors.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages describing AI policy or AI impacts.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the list is followed by a specific AI policy, code AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY as well.

examples.quote: blockchain, artificial intelligence, big-data analytics, biology, software development and programming

proposals.label: Human-centred, rights-based technology
proposals.definition: AI and technology must remain human-centred, rights-based and at the service of humanity, guided by social responsibility.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI must serve humanity, be human-centred, rights-based, or guided by social responsibility.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude human-rights passages (e.g. gender equality) that do not reference AI or technology.
proposals.boundary_cases: A sentence pairing opportunity with responsibility to keep AI human-centred also qualifies for AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.

examples.quote: it also creates a responsibility to ensure that technological transformation remains human-centered and rights-based
Technology should be an evolutionary gift to humanity, developed, founded, and guided with social responsibility, serving the greater good.

proposals.label: AI as opportunity and responsibility
proposals.definition: AI is explicitly framed as both an extraordinary opportunity and a source of risk or responsibility.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages explicitly contrasting AI's promise with its risks or duties.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages mentioning only risks or only benefits.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Safe, responsible, and inclusive' harnessing implies both sides but without explicit contrast; code only if opportunity is stated.

examples.quote: But AI presents not only an extraordinary opportunity, it also creates a responsibility

proposals.label: AI risks require multilateral response
proposals.definition: AI risks are presented as outpacing national frameworks, justifying stronger multilateralism and safe, responsible harnessing.
proposals.inclusion: Include statements that AI risks cannot be addressed by national frameworks alone or that AI must be harnessed safely and responsibly through collective action.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general UN reform arguments that do not cite AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: AI listed among global challenges (conflict, climate) as a reason for multilateralism counts here if risk speed is noted.

examples.quote: artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies are creating risks at a speed that national frameworks alone cannot adequately address
the rise of the artificial intelligence, must be harnessed in a safe, responsible, and inclusive manner

proposals.label: AI shaping young people's future
proposals.definition: AI is linked to education and future opportunities for young people and future generations.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages where AI is said to shape the opportunities of youth, students, or future generations.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude education passages with no AI reference.
proposals.boundary_cases: Brief mention of 'technology' choices affecting future generations without naming AI is borderline and should not be coded.

examples.quote: And artificial intelligence will increasingly shape those possibilities.

proposals.label: AI as both benefit and threat
proposals.definition: Explicit framing of AI (alone or with other emerging technologies) as capable of great benefit and serious harm, depending on human choices.
proposals.inclusion: Passages stating AI can bring enormous benefits but also inequality, manipulation or security risks, or that it 'can be a threat or a solution'.
proposals.exclusion: Passages that only list AI's effects without contrasting benefit and harm.
proposals.boundary_cases: Statements that AI 'can accelerate development, but' must remain within legal limits lean toward rights/governance unless harms are explicitly named.

examples.quote: It can bring enormous benefits to humanity, it can also deepen existing inequalities enable new forms of manipulation, and create security risks
Artificial intelligence, cyber capabilities, space technologies, robotics, each can be a threat or a solution. The choice is ours.

proposals.label: Rules and cooperation keeping pace with AI
proposals.definition: Calls for rules, safeguards, declarations or international cooperation to guide AI development.
proposals.inclusion: Passages urging rules and safeguards for AI or citing multilateral AI initiatives such as the Global Partnership on AI and ministerial declarations.
proposals.exclusion: UN-reform passages that do not connect to AI or technology governance.
proposals.boundary_cases: Security-focused emerging-technology governance without specific weapons references stays here rather than military.

examples.quote: Rules, safeguards, and cooperation must keep pace with innovation.
The Belgrade Ministerial Declaration received the support of 44 member states in the European Union and affirmed the need for safe, sustainable, and human-centered artificial intelligence.

proposals.label: AI bound by law, dignity, accountability
proposals.definition: AI use must respect human rights, human dignity, legal frameworks and democratic accountability; human-centred AI.
proposals.inclusion: Passages conditioning AI use on legal frameworks, human dignity, human rights or accountability.
proposals.exclusion: Passages about geopolitical rules of the international order unrelated to AI's own conduct.
proposals.boundary_cases: A chairmanship priority list including human rights and the digital divide may be coded here and with governance.

examples.quote: its use must remain consistent with legal frameworks, human dignity and democratic accountability
technological progress remained connected with security, human rights, the rule of law, accountability, and bridging the digital divide

proposals.label: Technological power without political wisdom
proposals.definition: Argument that AI-driven technological advancement will not by itself make the world safer unless international order and principles are upheld.
proposals.inclusion: Passages contrasting advanced AI capability with a deteriorating or unpredictable political/international order.
proposals.exclusion: Passages about AI regulation specifically rather than the broader international order.
proposals.boundary_cases: Future-looking passages listing AI among forces reshaping the world count here when they pivot to the need for a stable international order.

examples.quote: It will merely make us more technologically advanced in a world that is becoming politically less predictable.
technological capability does not automatically produce political wisdom

proposals.label: AI transforming professions and industries
proposals.definition: AI described as transforming the economy, professions, labour markets and decision-making.
proposals.inclusion: Passages stating AI will change professions, industries, the labour market or how states function.
proposals.exclusion: Passages naming AI only as a symbol of technological advancement.
proposals.boundary_cases: Broad lists of AI's effects across economy, education and medicine can be coded here when labour/professions are named.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence will transform professions, industries, and the ways in which decisions are made.
Artificial intelligence is already changing the economy, education, medicine, security, the labor market, and the way states function.

proposals.label: Passing, incidental AI reference
proposals.definition: AI is mentioned only incidentally or in passing, without substantive discussion of AI.
proposals.inclusion: Fragmentary or incidental references (e.g. naming an AI institute) where the passage's argument is about something else.
proposals.exclusion: Any passage that discusses AI's effects, risks or governance.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the mention is followed by any claim about AI's impact, code the substantive theme instead.

examples.quote: the artificial intelligence institute, because it is a natural thing that I protect its interests

proposals.label: AI listed among global challenges
proposals.definition: AI named in a list of interconnected global challenges requiring multilateralism, without further elaboration.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages where AI appears only as one item in a list of global challenges or issues.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that elaborate AI's role, risks or governance.
proposals.boundary_cases: If the list is followed by specific AI discussion, code the substantive theme instead.

examples.quote: global challenges from conflicts and terrorism to climate change, artificial intelligence and economic insecurity are not only complex, but also deeply interconnected

proposals.label: Technology at service of humanity
proposals.definition: Technology and AI must serve humanity, guided by ethical standards and human rights, with human intelligence and compassion prioritized over AI.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages stressing human values, ethics and rights over or alongside AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude national digitization achievements without ethical framing.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for international cooperation on the digital age may also be AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: The problems of this world cannot be solved by artificial intelligence alone. but by human intelligence and compassion.
The digital age must be guided by international cooperation, ethical standards, and respect for human rights.

proposals.label: AI listed among multiplying global challenges
proposals.definition: AI is named briefly in a list of global challenges or threats (conflict, climate, migration, inequality) without further discussion of AI itself.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages where AI appears only as one item in an enumeration of global challenges or threats.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages that go on to discuss AI's specific risks, uses or governance.
proposals.boundary_cases: Lists of technologies (rather than challenges) go to AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION; the phrase 'unchecked rise' signals mild concern but not substantive discussion.

examples.quote: rising inequality or even the unchecked rise of artificial intelligence, those challenges jeopardize our present and our future
Climate change, migration, the advent of artificial intelligence. Our world is changing.

proposals.label: AI among new challenges alongside fake news
proposals.definition: AI named among new challenges (with fake news and cyberthreats) as causing major changes, without further elaboration.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages briefly listing AI among emerging challenges without substantive discussion.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages developing specific AI risks or policies.
proposals.boundary_cases: A follow-on generic call for a joint pact does not make it substantive governance unless AI rules are discussed.

examples.quote: Some others, although of newer date, such as artificial intelligence, are already causing major changes in our lives.

proposals.label: Joint pact needed for new challenges
proposals.definition: General assertion that no country can respond alone to new challenges including AI, requiring a joint pact for the future.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages stating AI-related challenges require collective/multilateral responses.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages with no collective-response claim.
proposals.boundary_cases: Reference to the Pact for the Future could also fit AI_UN_ROLE if the UN instrument is explicit.

examples.quote: without a joint pact for the future, no country or group of countries will have the potential to offer or implement responses to those challenges alone

proposals.label: AI-driven autonomous warfare and drones
proposals.definition: AI discussed as transforming warfare, including autonomous drones, AI deciding on the battlefield, and an AI arms race.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages describing AI in weapons, autonomous drones, battlefield decision-making, or calls for rules on AI in weapons.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude drone warfare discussion that makes no link to AI or autonomy.
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for global rules on AI weapons should also be coded AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE; speculative claims about AI 'shaping atoms' tied to war fit here.

examples.quote: We need global rules now for how AI can be used in weapons, and this is just as urgent as preventing the spread of nuclear weapons.
there is already a real possibility that AI, not only people, will begin will begin decide what happens on the battlefield
Artificial intelligence could be trained to fight well before it would learn to help humankind.

proposals.label: AI escalation as looming global threat
proposals.definition: AI framed as an approaching threshold of danger for humanity requiring peace before AI capabilities advance further.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages warning that advancing AI capability creates a civilizational-level threat or deadline for action.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude narrowly tactical descriptions of AI weapons without broader warning.
proposals.boundary_cases: Where the threat is purely battlefield-specific, prefer AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS alone.

examples.quote: one day AI will move from the digital world to shaping atoms. And when that happens, we had better be at peace.

proposals.label: Agile regulation and sandboxes for AI
proposals.definition: AI as outpacing regulation, with the speaker promoting agile national rules such as regulatory sandboxes.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages about national regulatory approaches to keep pace with AI, e.g., sandboxes and adaptive rules.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude calls for international AI governance frameworks.
proposals.boundary_cases: National AI investment claims without regulatory focus belong to AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

examples.quote: Technology is moving faster than regulation almost everywhere, and artificial intelligence is widening that gap.

proposals.label: National AI talent and industries
proposals.definition: Speaker presents national capabilities or workforce in AI as an asset for investment.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages showcasing national specialists, industries or investment in AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages discussing AI only as a global risk.
proposals.boundary_cases: If AI appears only in a list of industries, also consider AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION.

examples.quote: are shaping the industries of the future, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, defense technologies, advanced manufacturing and robotics

proposals.label: UN centrality and lag on AI
proposals.definition: The UN as the central forum for AI rules and cooperation, or criticism that the UN is failing to keep pace with AI and technological change.
proposals.inclusion: Passages asserting the UN's special responsibility for AI, welcoming the Global Dialogue/Scientific Panel, or saying new AI initiatives outside the UN show it is lagging.
proposals.exclusion: Generic calls for rules without reference to the UN (use AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
proposals.boundary_cases: Citing China's global AI cooperation organization as evidence of UN failure counts here.

examples.quote: The UN shoulders a special responsibility given the fast-paced development of AI technologies.
the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, China's project, this confirms that the UN is failing to recognize new trends
How do we enable our international institutions to keep pace with the technologies that are reshaping our world?

proposals.label: AI within international information security regime
proposals.definition: AI regulation framed within the state-centric international information security agenda, alongside cybercrime conventions and responsible state behaviour rules, with equal participation of all countries.
proposals.inclusion: Passages linking AI rules to international information security, cybercrime conventions or legally binding digital-arena agreements.
proposals.exclusion: AI governance calls not framed through information security (use AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
proposals.boundary_cases: Calls for generally recognized AI rules with equal participation in an information-security context take this and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: developing generally acceptable approaches to regulating the digital arena and understanding the processes related to the development of artificial intelligence
Generally recognized rules for the use of AI should be underpinned on an equal foundation with the participation of all countries.

proposals.label: AI listed among global challenges
proposals.definition: AI named in a list of global challenges or pressures on the order without further elaboration.
proposals.inclusion: Passages where AI appears alongside climate, inequality or peace as a list item, or as a vague technological revolution.
proposals.exclusion: Passages that develop an argument about AI specifically.
proposals.boundary_cases: A generic reference to forces of technological revolution with no AI term is only included if the cluster context is AI.

examples.quote: peace and security, climate change and environmental destruction, artificial intelligence and growing inequalities

proposals.label: AI misuse as hybrid security threat
proposals.definition: AI treated as an emerging security threat alongside hybrid attacks, cyber attacks and sabotage, especially misuse by hostile or malign actors.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages listing AI misuse among emerging or hybrid threats, or warning that AI in the wrong hands becomes a tool of disruption and conflict.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude passages about autonomous weapons or AI in military command systems, which belong to AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.
proposals.boundary_cases: Where the harm is specifically disinformation/information manipulation, also code AI_DISINFORMATION.

examples.quote: Emerging threats like climate change, cyber attacks, hybrid attacks, and the misuse of artificial intelligence are testing us on a daily basis.
But in the wrong hands, it can also become a powerful tool for deception, disruption, and conflict.
As any instrument, AI is also increasingly used by those seeking to cause harm and destruction.

proposals.label: AI safety and loss of control
proposals.definition: Concern with the safety of AI systems, including warnings that control of AI could slip out of human hands.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages naming AI safety as a security priority or warning of loss of human control over AI.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude general misuse-by-bad-actors framing without a safety or control concern.
proposals.boundary_cases: 'Make it safer' in a pro-innovation passage counts only if safety is an explicit goal rather than a passing adjective.

examples.quote: With even major technology companies sending warning signals that control of AI might slip out of humanity's hands, the time is ripe for collective action.
These include climate change, hybrid threats, the challenges related to the safety of artificial intelligence.

proposals.label: AI amplifying disinformation and manipulation
proposals.definition: AI linked to disinformation, foreign information manipulation, and attacks on information integrity.
proposals.inclusion: Include passages stating AI enhances disinformation or manipulation risks, or linking AI misuse concerns with media literacy and disinformation resilience.
proposals.exclusion: Exclude disinformation passages that never connect to AI.
proposals.boundary_cases: A passage on disinformation resilience followed by a generic AI misuse concern counts when adjacent sentences connect them.

examples.quote: This risk is further enhanced by the development of artificial intelligence.
Latvia has meaningful experience in building resilience to disinformation and promoting media literacy.

It is our collective responsibility to ensure that this technology serves human dignity. This is particularly urgent because technologies are already changing the foundations of our societies. AI is not waiting for our institutions to catch up. Our institutions have to catch up with AI. At the beginning of my remarks, I asked three questions: Who controls new technologies? Who sets the rules? And who is accountable? We cannot answer them by simply trusting that those with the greatest capabilities will always act in the interest of everyone else. These requirements should be supported by effective national and regional oversight. At the same time, we need to ensure accountability, in particular when global peace and security are potentially affected. In the course of this week, we have intensified our conversation about these questions. How we address AI together is one of the clearest tests whether we have the strength and the will to build a United Nations for today's world. The next Secretary-General can count on Germany along this path. Our history, our geography and our constitution bind us to the UN Charter and to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. This is at the very core of our statehood. The technologies may change, but one principle will remain. Power must be bound by responsibility and progress must serve human dignity. The world has long been in a mode of permanent escalation and with it, the UN is navigating stormy waters. We must decide. Are we truly willing to let the boat we all share drift toward capsizing, or will we pool our strengths and steer it back on course? The tools are in our hands. Together, we can push for renewal and build a peaceful future for generations to come. I thank you.

Mr. President, Excellencies, Distinguished Delegates, Allow me to begin by congratulating you, Dr. Rahman, on your election as President of the General Assembly. you can count on Latvia's support. Accession negotiations are underway and we are moving quickly. Our ambition is clear, to anchor Moldova firmly in the European family. Mr. President, Mr. Secretary General, Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, a child who will sit at a school desk for the first time this autumn will, in 2040, be a young person just entering adulthood. We do not know exactly what the world in which that young person will live will look like, but we already know that it will be different from our own. Artificial intelligence will transform professions, industries, and the ways in which decisions are made. Energy will be governed by a new configuration and a new logic of operation. Climate change will affect economies, agriculture, cities, and the movement of people. Demographic change will reshape labor markets and social protection systems. Security will no longer depend on armies and borders, but also on power grids, data centers, cables, satellites, algorithms, and trust in the information we receive every day. And yet today, as we prepare for the future, millions of people are living through war or under the threat of war. More than 100 million people have been displaced by force. More than 270 million children and young people are not in the school. This is the paradox of our time. Humanity has never possessed such immense scientific and technological capabilities. And yet, it has never been more evident that technological capability does not automatically produce political wisdom. That is why the real question before this assembly is not simply how we will manage the crisis of 2026. The real question is this. What kind of international order will leave to the generations that is entering school today? For a small size country like mine, this is not an academic question. It is a question of survival. 33 years ago, since we become a part of the United Nations, the world looked very different. The Cold War had ended. There was hope that a new era was beginning, an era in which cooperation would gradually replace confrontation. Our region, however, was living through a very different reality. Yugoslavia was disintegrating in bloodshed. Wars were being fought just beyond our borders.

Montenegro is a reliable, credible and predictable partner, committed to an effective multilateral system with the UN Charter at its core, aligned with the European Union's Common Foreign and Security Policy, and working closely with our NATO Allies and EU partners in support of international peace and security. And this commitment comes at a time when the United Nations itself is facing a profound test. Eight decades after its foundation, the challenges confronting this organization are increasingly complex and interconnected. Conflicts are eroding trust in the international system. Climate change is testing the resilience of states and of societies, and artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies are creating risks at a speed that national frameworks alone cannot adequately address. So the answer cannot be less multilateralism. It must be more effective multilateralism. And Montenegro, therefore, strongly supports the UN reform agenda and the ambition to build a United Nations that is more effective, more agile, more accessible, more financially sustainable and fit for the challenges of our time. This reform must strengthen the UN's ability to deliver where it matters most. in preventing conflict, protecting human rights and freedoms, advancing sustainable development, and responding effectively to humanitarian crises. This responsibility also extends to the Security Council itself, which must become more effective, representative, accountable, and transparent. And the exercise of the veto must carry the weight of conscience Above all, when the world is confronted with mass atrocities and the large-scale loss of civilian life, the Charter of the United Nations must remain our common reference point. And Montenegro will be a constructive partner in those efforts. Excellencies, Montenegro remains committed to supporting Ukraine and welcomes all credible diplomatic efforts aimed at bringing the war to this end. We believe that a just and lasting peace must be achieved through dialogue and diplomacy. In Gaza, our responsibility begins with the protection of human lives. Civilians must be protected and humanitarian assistance must reach those in need safely and without any obstruction. Israelis deserve lasting security. And Palestinians deserve dignity, freedom and a viable state of their own.

They become stronger by building institutions in which every single citizen can recognize the same fairness and the same dignity. Excellencies, the choices we make today, choices on peace, technology, and climate action will shape the lives of generations yet to come. The Pact for the Future reminds us of precisely this responsibility. that the decisions we make today must not undermine the possibilities of those who will live with their consequences tomorrow. But future generations should not only be the subject of our decisions, they should have a voice in making them. And Montenegro has heard the call from the young people to move from participation to real influence in decision making. Young people are not simply beneficiaries of public policy, they are partners in shaping it. And education, education is our most powerful investment in young people, equipping them with knowledge, with critical thinking, with values they need to shape a better world. And this is very personal to me as well. I know what education can make possible. I was born and educated in Montenegro. And it was education, education which gave me the opportunity to study and work abroad, to learn from other countries, from other institutions, and to ultimately return home to serve my own country. It shaped my belief that the place where a child is born should never define the limits of what that child can become. Coming from a small country, one can sometimes assume that greater size brings greater vision and greater wisdom. But the United Nations reminds us of a simple truth: Vision and wisdom are not measured by the size of a country, but by the ideas we bring and the responsibility with which we act upon. And our responsibility is to expand those possibilities, to build schools that inspire, institutions that recognize talent, economies that reward ideas and work, and societies in which young people have a reason to stay and those who left have a reason to return. And artificial intelligence will increasingly shape those possibilities.

But AI presents not only an extraordinary opportunity, it also creates a responsibility to ensure that technological transformation remains human-centered and rights-based. Technology must remain at the service of humanity and not the other way around. Climate change demands the same long-term responsibility. Montenegro carries the identity and responsibility of an ecological state. Our mountains, our rivers, our forests, and the Adriatic Sea are not simply natural resources. They are part of our national identity and of the legacy we will leave to our future generations. But climate change is also a question of global fairness, because those who have contributed the least to this crisis are too often the first and hardest hit by its consequences. And no country can solve this challenge alone. This is one of the clearest reasons why effective multilateralism remains indispensable. Excellencies, to conclude, 20 years ago, Montenegro entered this very hall at the beginning of a new chapter in our history. We have built our institutions, secured our place on the global stage, strengthened our economy, strengthened our democracy, and brought our country within reach of membership in the European Union. Our transformation is not complete, but its direction is very clear. And when the next generation of Montenegro stands in this hall 20 years from now, I hope they will be able to say that we used our moment well, that Montenegro completed successfully its European journey, that our region, the Balkans, left all divisions behind, and that we stood firmly in defense of the rules and principles that protect peace in the world. But above all, I hope they will be able to say something much simpler, that we gave them more opportunities than we had ourselves. Because that is ultimately the responsibility of leadership, not simply to manage the present, but to expand the possibilities of the future. At the beginning of my address, I spoke about the meaning we attach to keeping one's word. And perhaps this is also what the United Nations needs most today.

Romania's evolution over the past 37 years proves the crucial importance of upholding these principles. Millions of Romanians known from their personal experience the difference between a communist system that oppressed them and stifled their initiative and freedom of choice and a democracy that rewards work, innovation, and personal responsibility. This choice has turned Romania into one of Europe's most dynamic destinations in Europe for investment and industrial development. Romania has aligned itself with the standards of the OECD. Leading global companies have established manufacturing, engineering, technology, and service centers in my country, attracted by our conducive business environment and highly skilled workforce. Next year, we will begin extracting, exploiting 100 billion cubic meters of natural gas in the Black Sea. Romania is a gateway between Europe and the rest of the world, located at the intersection of the Danube, the Black Sea, and major trade corridors. My country serves as strategic hub for trade, energy and transport. Economic growth is all the stronger when it is based on partnership. Our message is simple. Ladies and gentlemen, we have entered the fifth year of the illegal, unprovoked, and unjustified full-scale war of aggression against Ukraine waged by a permanent member of the Security Council. We are promoting an agenda which we can all get behind, a unifying agenda, concrete ideas and projects. Today, what's coming to the fore is the topic of international information security. The start of the work of the Global Dialogue on AI Governance and the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, we believe these are steps in the right direction. In the middle of the previous century, the USSR helped peoples in Africa, Asia, and Latin America to free themselves from colonial dependence. A key milestone on this path was the adoption by the General Assembly of a resolution proclaiming the 14th of December an International Day against colonialism in all of its forms and manifestations. We would be delighted to see supporters of this fight against neocolonialism, to partake in an international inter-party movement. The first assembly of the For Freedom of Nations Summit will take place in Russia in the coming months. Colleagues, ensuring lasting peace is only possible if the main players in the global stage stop competing. This is only possible if we meticulously uphold the charter and the principle of equal and indivisible security. This principle, I'd like to remind you, means not to further the security of one state at the expense of the security of others. Also, no countries nor any groups of countries should try to dominate the security sphere.

The Security Council is often blocked precisely in the crisis in which it should be most active. Other parts of the UN system face financial pressures, overlapping mandates, bureaucratization, and the justified demand of member states to see more concrete results. These are real problems, and there is no benefit in glossing over them. Yet it by no means follows that we need the United Nations less. We may need it more than ever. It simply must be more effective, more focused, and more prepared to address the issues for which it was created. Over the past eight decades, states have not come to this building because they share the same interests, but because they understood that the cost of settling disagreements by force of arms was too high. That is why multilateralism came into being and why we are here today. Serbia supports the United Nations and reform of the UN system, so that the organization may become more effective and better adapted to today's realities. We advocate a more representative UNSC through greater representation of developing countries, particularly those from the African continent, as well as more inclusive regional representation and the addition of another seat for the Eastern European group. However, without a genuine return to the principles on which we have already agreed, I do not expect progress in terms of this organization's concrete results. Excellencies, peace is not the only test of our ability to manage change. We are in the midst of a technological transformation whose full reach we are only beginning to understand. Artificial intelligence is already changing the economy, education, medicine, security, the labor market, and the way states function. It can bring enormous benefits to humanity, it can also deepen existing inequalities enable new forms of manipulation, and create security risks that we could not even have imagined only a few years ago.

During our leadership cycle in the Global Partnership of Artificial Intelligence, which Serbia chaired in 2025, one of our priorities was to ensure that technological progress remained connected with security, human rights, the rule of law, accountability, and bridging the digital divide. The Belgrade Ministerial Declaration received the support of 44 member states in the European Union and affirmed the need for safe, sustainable, and human-centered artificial intelligence. The more powerful technology becomes, the more responsible those who manage it must be. We may have cutting-edge algorithms, quantum computers, unmanned systems, and artificial intelligence capable of processing in a matter of seconds. what once took us years. But if at the same time we allow the fundamental rules of the international order to be applied selectively, technological progress will not make the world safer. It will merely make us more technologically advanced in a world that is becoming politically less predictable. If we wish to manage the coming transformation responsibly, we must first reinforce the foundation on which the international order rests. Those foundations are simple. the sovereign equality of states, respect for territorial integrity, the prohibition of the use of force except in the cases expressly provided for in the UN Charter, and the obligation not to change the rules from one case to another. Esteemed colleagues, to those of you who know Serbia and our region, as well as those less familiar with this part of the world, I wish to express my gratitude to all who have honored Serbia by confirming their participation in the specialized exhibition Expo 2027 to be held next year in Belgrade under the theme Play for Humanity, Sport and Music for All. Culture, science, sport, technology, business, and young people from all parts of the world will come together in Belgrade, and I look forward to our hosting a large number of the states represented in this hall today. At the outset, I spoke about trust and responsibility. And that is where I wish to conclude. We will not restore trust through grand declarations if we then continue to act as before.

Ukrainians understand that this winter could be very harsh for us, but in response, we will have no choice but to make it painful for Russia too. And that's exactly why we say that de-escalation steps important, are needed before winter, now. We need diplomacy and we need strength. And step by step, we are closing the gaps in both. Yesterday, we met with the President of the United States, and this is exactly what we discussed. Unfortunately, we have not had a chance to speak directly with the leader of China, who is in America today, but not here. And he is someone who can influence Russia, too, more than many, many others can. And we would like him to want peace as much as we do in Ukraine. We believe the world has the power to make this happen. We are sure the world needs this. This is about energy, about critical infrastructure. This is about food security. This is about the lives of many, many people in many countries. And this is about finally slowing down the rapid development of weapons for killing, a process that has continued throughout this war and has already become a global threat. We need to slow it down before we reach the next stage, because as early as next year, there is already a real possibility that AI, not only people, will begin will begin decide what happens on the battlefield. And we need peace before we reach that point. Ladies and gentlemen, Russia's leader, patient zero, the man from whom this war began and spread into the world, becoming the largest war in Europe since World War II, will inevitably leave this world. But the longer Putin is able to wage war, the more evil he will leave behind in this world. Today, nothing in war works the same way it did, by the way, in 2022, except the courage of people. Everything has changed. And who knows whether courage will still work the same way in the future.

If you listen to some of the biggest believers in the development of AI, they say today AI still remains mostly digital, but one day AI will move from the digital world to shaping atoms. And when that happens, we had better be at peace. We certainly need to end the wars that already exist. Ukraine deserves security, just as all of you do, every country and every nation. And one more thing. For weeks, for weeks now, Europeans have warned that Russia may go further into Europe, even into NATO territory. Leaders have intelligence showing Russian intentions. And right now, I want to speak not to Europe. I want to speak to those countries whose people Russia may try to use in another absolutely brutal campaign. We have had more than just North Korean POWs. We know that Russia uses citizens of 47 countries in its war, in this war. Ghana, Nepal, Tajikistan, India, Yemen, Kenya, Zimbabwe, Cuba, Belarus, Sudan, South Africa, and many, many others. And from time to time, we receive requests to send particular POWs back home. And through the videos from our drones, we also see people dying on the battlefield who are not Russians, people from your countries, 47 countries who ended up in Russia through deception and tricks. So I want to speak directly to every representative of these 47 countries. You know what Russia is doing with your people, your citizens. Take care of them and do not let them end up on another front. Do not let Putin drag you into this war. Do not let Russia put out its fires, cover up its shame, and pay for its madness with the lives of your people. Limit his room to act, limit his money, limit his war. And please, everyone here, do not be the last to join those who defend life, be the first to say we guaranteed security. Thank you, everyone who helps. And thank you to everyone who stands with us, with our people, with our children, with Ukraine.
